brief.scope: Independently review the exact seven-document candidate, five final interface dispositions and adoption unit1a couplings. Read current AGENTS.md, ops/README.md, founding contracts, supplied ruling and original records. Verify trusted selection/scope/declaration/dependency/output-attempt/result.policy transport, ID reservation/admission ordering, late refusal, evaluate_tool counterpart, preserved brief.policy and dev/prod separation. findings.claim: The conductor launch identity is unsatisfiable under the enumerations it binds to. Declared (startup): "`DispatchID` is the canonical execution record's `id` ... `<UTC stamp>-<stage>-<harness>-<6 hex>`" and "`launch_id` equals that record's id byte-for-byte ... Model observations, custody and receipts resolve through that record ... Refuse a mismatched record/descriptor binding before effects" (conductor-start-plan.md:352-359). Practiced in the record's own owner: "`--stage` is one of `plan`, `tests`, `check-tests`, `code`, `review`, `adjudicate`" (ops/devlane/dispatch/CONTRACT.md:394-395) and the record carries "role (read|write)" (CONTRACT.md:684). The only text joining the two is "Conductor startup uses its separately declared LaunchSelection and the same canonical DispatchID reservation duty, without inventing a worker job binding" (CONTRACT.md:830), which extends neither enumeration. LaunchSelection is `role:"conductor", job_role:null` (conductor-start-plan.md:365-367), so a conduct launch has no admissible `<stage>` segment and no admissible record `role`. An independent implementer must either label a conduct launch with one of the six worker stages — the worker job binding the same sentence forbids — or violate the id grammar the descriptor pins byte-for-byte. This is the same namespace-incompatibility shape as the original p2 the branch was opened to fix, one level down.

The grants_sha256 edge has no declared derivation from its producing endpoint, so independent producers cannot recompute the same bytes. Declared (consumer): "For `grants_sha256`, normalize exactly `{scope,job,role,adapter,outputs,maintenance}`. The first five values are closed `{repository:[path,...],outputs:[relative-output-path,...]}` sets" (lane-policy.md:410-412). Declared (producer): "`LaunchDeclarations` is exactly `{selection,requested_scope,job_grants,role_grants,adapter_grants,outputs,reservations,sources}`", where "`requested_scope`, `job_grants`, `role_grants` and `adapter_grants` each have exactly `{repository,outputs}`" and "`outputs` is precisely the validated C2 array" (ops/devlane/task/CONTRACT.md:459-460, 478-479, 491). Two gaps: the four producing grant keys are renamed to four normalized keys with no stated mapping — `grep -c` for job_grants/requested_scope in lane-policy.md and dispatch/CONTRACT.md is 0 in all four cases — and the fifth normalized value, a `{repository,outputs}` set with "`outputs.repository` is empty" (line 415), has no `{repository,outputs}` counterpart in LaunchDeclarations at all; its only candidate source is the C2 declaration array, a different closed type under the same key name. PolicyResult requires "the independently recomputed binding" (line 507) and the consumer "recomputes this binding from admitted sources before each transition" (line 325), so a missing derivation rule produces digest disagreement and refusal between conforming implementations. The supplied checker does not detect this: it constructs `normalized = {k: scope for k in ['scope','job','role','adapter','outputs']}` by fiat (check_unit1a_docs.py:87-88) instead of deriving it from `declarations`, and so assigns the grant-set shape to `outputs` while assigning the C2 array to `declarations['outputs']` in the same script (line 81).

findings.claim: `result.policy` is now described twice in one file with different member types and a different member count, and the earlier description was not updated. Declared (pre-existing, retained): "Acceptance evidence is launcher-produced `result.policy`: the full `brief.policy` binding, checked snapshot ref, result head, SHA-256 of the measured artifact manifest and dependency evidence, check time and outcome" (lines 347-350) — eight members, artifacts and dependencies as bare digests, no outputs. Declared (new): "PolicyResult is exactly `{binding,snapshot_ref,head,artifacts,dependencies,outputs,checked_at,outcome,refusal}`" where "artifacts/dependencies/outputs are verified retained handles", handles being "exactly `{path,sha256}`" (lines 495-503, 442) — nine members, three handle objects. dispatch/CONTRACT.md:916-917 makes PolicyResult authoritative ("`result.policy` is exactly policy's PolicyResult"), but the new section states "C1/C2 and the accepted policy binding above retain their schemas and owners" (line 364), which points a reader back at the superseded shape. One of the two must be corrected or explicitly marked superseded.

The normative sentence that defines when the late-refusal rule fires is a run-on spliced across an unrewrapped orphan line. Practiced: line 537 "After launch preparation, an attempt or verification has acted, failure of a", line 538 the four-word orphan "required policy check", line 539 "is a late refusal: ...". Read as one sentence it is "After launch preparation, an attempt or verification has acted, failure of a required policy check is a late refusal" — a comma splice in which the trigger condition (after launch preparation, or after an attempt has acted?) is left ambiguous in the one place that separates exit 2 from Abort 3. This is the same splice shape as the fill finding the recheck raised (20260906T110711Z-review-claude-e4968e, finding 5), which was otherwise closed: conductor-start-plan.md:85-95 and probes-lever.md:155/329 are now rewrapped, and lane-policy.md:538 is the residue in new text.

The job's own scope required two commits and one landed. Declared: "use separate commits for fixes and unit1a" (ag-conduct-interfaces-final.json, brief.scope). Practiced: one commit carries all seven documents (git diff --name-only 4738d74 f15ca22 lists exactly the seven), and the message discloses the cause and points at out/: "Separate patches and clean messages for the requested two commits are retained in out as 01-interface-fix.patch with 01-COMMIT_MSG and 02-unit1a.patch with 02-COMMIT_MSG." Those artifacts live only in the dispatch job directory, not in the repository, so the separation the scope asked for leaves no durable evidence once the job directory is reaped; the citation is a dangling reference from a permanent commit into transient state. The cause (read-only .git) is honestly recorded and the ruling forbids rewriting history, so the remedy is to retain the two patches as a record or ladder input, not to re-commit.

UNIT1A COUPLINGS, WHAT HELD. Transport is declared in both directions and every new local link resolves. CHECKS I EXECUTED. sha256sum of all seven documents; git rev-parse of three trees; git diff --name-only, --numstat and --binary|sha256sum; git diff --check over 710dbac..f15ca22, which produced no output; git log -1 --format=%B on f15ca22; grep counts of json fences (1+2+1+0 in the four startup docs = 4; 4+0+0 in the three unit1a docs; 8 total, matching all_json_examples), evaluate_tool occurrences (lane-policy 1, permission-surface 2), brief.policy occurrences, the new anchors (all six unit1a headings and #the-job-directory exist at the cited lines), the closed --stage and role enumerations, the lane-* refusal class table, and outputs-custody (declared pre-existing at dispatch:305, not an undeclared class). Line-fill measured with grep '.\{85,\}' and '.\{95,\}'.

RECEIPT AND CHECKER LIMITATIONS, DECLARED. I could not execute either successor checker: this profile refuses arbitrary python3 invocation, and the checkers are path-coupled to the dispatch job layout (root = __file__/../../snapshot) and write interface-successor.json, unit1a-synthetic-examples.json and startup-couplings-checks.json into their own directory, which is in/ here — running them would mutate supplied inputs. So the receipt's counts were compared against the documents by grep and by reading the checker source, not re-executed; four of its digest fields (files_sha256 x7, checked_worktree_tree, worktree_diff_sha256, head_tree) were reproduced by other means and all matched. check_unit1a_docs.py imports the third-party jsonschema and exec-loads ops/devlane/dispatch/record.py; I could not confirm jsonschema is installed here, and the lane's instrument convention is stdlib only (ops/conductor/instrument-conventions.md:52), so this checker is not a stdlib-reproducible artifact even where python3 is permitted. The historical checker in/check_interfaces.py was not supplied to this job; its digest 11d1af3fa58eb40e0a1b0dc9c8dad25b07f3c189b65e9186bb177426adbc88aa matches the receipt's historical_checker_sha256 and the final job's input listing, but I could not read its line 138 and therefore cannot independently confirm that its failure is the evaluate_tool absence assertion — that claim rests on the producer's record and on the fact that unit1a's mandated addition necessarily breaks any absence assertion over it. Consistent with the supplied ruling I treat that checker as evidence of the prior phase and not as a current acceptance requirement, and I did not touch the worker's invalid status or the historical receipt. The ten loopstrap remote links are historical and unfetched — no network in this profile. No repository, test, settings, host, state or admission write; no probe, suite or vendor launch; nothing here admits a harness, activates policy, or approves security or live capability, which remains separately owned.
